text: {"rulings": [{"id": "1", "relation": "unrelated", "reason": "httpOnly and sameSite=strict are independent cookie attributes; a cookie can carry both, so both claims stand."}, {"id": "2", "relation": "refines", "reason": "Auth using session cookies is the broader fact; sameSite=strict adds detail about how those cookies are configured without contradicting it."}, {"id": "3", "relation": "unrelated", "reason": "Redis backing is about where session data is stored, while sameSite=strict is a browser cookie attribute; both can be true at once."}, {"id": "4", "relation": "unrelated", "reason": "Rate limiting has nothing to do with the sameSite setting on session cookies."}, {"id": "5", "relation": "unrelated", "reason": "The language of the Meridian stack is unaffected by how session cookies are configured."}]}
